reports.text:
Indication: Alzheimer disease, follow-up.
Comparison: 08/2021.
Technique: axial noncontrast CT of the head.
Findings: Diffuse sulcal and ventricular prominence, with volume loss most pronounced in the medial temporal lobes and the hippocampi bilaterally. No hemorrhage, infarct, mass or extra-axial fluid. No hydrocephalus out of proportion to atrophy.
reports.conclusion: Generalized cerebral atrophy with disproportionate medial temporal and hippocampal volume loss. No acute intracranial process.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 02/18/2022

Mrs. Pratt returns with her daughter six months after her initial cognitive evaluation of August 2021.

Interval: Recent events slip away more - appointments, what was said on the phone. She misplaces things more often than in the summer and now pauses mid-sentence hunting for words. Still lives alone and still pays her own bills. Not driving.

Medications per list: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81. NKDA.

Exam: Alert, oriented to person and place, not to date. MMSE 24/30 (lost points: orientation, recall, serial 7s). Speech fluent with intact comprehension and repetition. No focal findings.

Imaging: repeat noncontrast head CT today shows generalized atrophy, most marked in the medial temporal lobes and hippocampi.

Impression: Alzheimer disease. Score today a little higher than in August, within the range of session-to-session variation; history indicates continued slow progression. Imaging pattern supports the diagnosis.

Plan: supervision of finances discussed with daughter. Return in 6 months.

Neurology

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. February neurology letter reviewed - MMSE 24, CT shows medial temporal atrophy; diagnosis unchanged.
Daughter notes snacks in place of lunch some days; weight down another kilo.
Exam: vitals as charted; soft SEM; lungs clear; feet intact, no lesions.
A1c 7.6 today - up a little; with her eating irregular I would not push harder on sugars. Continue metformin.
BP fine on lisinopril.
RTC June for wellness visit.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requests switch to blister packs for all four meds per daughter's request. New 90-day scripts sent for lisinopril 10, metformin 1000, simvastatin 20; aspirin OTC included in pack. Hydrochlorothiazide NOT included - on intolerance list.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV 2022, daughter present and helped with the questionnaire.

Function: bathes, dresses and feeds herself. Daughter now handles medications (blister packs), bill paying is being shared. Not driving. No falls; uses the handrail on stairs. PHQ-2 negative. Hearing adequate.

Cognition: known Alzheimer disease, followed by neurology.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight continues slow drift down. Soft systolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Feet: intact sensation and pulses. Skin fine.

Prevention: Tdap given today (last 2012). Now 75 - no further colonoscopy (normal 2014) or mammography (last 2020 negative); daughter and pt agree. DXA 2018 normal. Pneumococcal and shingles complete.

Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, urine albumin.
RTC 6 months; neurology in August.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY
Date of service: 08/29/2022

Mrs. Pratt, 75, with Alzheimer disease first evaluated in this clinic 07/2021 [sic, 08/2021] and again 02/2022, comes with her daughter for scheduled reassessment; I am seeing her for the first time, taking over from my colleague.

Daughter's account: across the past year her mother loses the thread of conversations, mislays things constantly and can no longer keep her accounts straight - the daughter has taken over the checkbook. Before she gave up the car she had become lost more than once on routes she had driven for decades. She lives alone and still sets out her own pills from the blister packs.

Meds as listed by referral: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81. NKDA.

Exam: BP 140/85. Neatly dressed and groomed. Mildly disoriented to time. Recalls 0 of 3 words at 5 minutes; serial 7s labored. MMSE 22/30. Motor and sensory exam nonfocal.

Labs today: fasting glucose 160. CBC, electrolytes, renal function and TSH normal.

Assessment: Alzheimer disease with gradual progression; now needs help with finances.
Plan: daughter to increase daily check-ins. Home safety reviewed. Return 1 year, sooner if behavior changes. Fasting glucose forwarded to PCP.

Neurology

documents.title: Neurology visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Jean's daughter writing from her account. Neurology said her fasting sugar was 160 and to let you know. Does she need to change anything? She also told them she is still on the water pill again, which she is not.

documents.title: RE: Neurology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the heads up. One fasting value of 160 doesn't change anything by itself - her A1c in March was 7.6, and we'll recheck in December. And you're right, she has been off hydrochlorothiazide since 2020; their list is out of date. No changes for now.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter with pt. High-dose flu R arm, bivalent Moderna L arm. Both tolerated, observed 15 minutes.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Exam 11/8/2022. VA cc 20/30 OU. Posterior chamber IOLs stable. Dilated fundus without diabetic retinopathy OU. Patient needed help with instructions during testing; daughter present. Recall 1 year.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Daughter completed HRA with her.

Function: independent in bathing, dressing, eating; daughter handles finances, medications, shopping and transport. Lives alone with a daily visit and a neighbor lunch twice weekly. No falls. No longer drinks any alcohol. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: weight 65, slow decline. Heart: soft SEM. Lungs clear. Feet normal. Gait steady.

Prevention up to date for age; screening stopped at 75 as agreed.
Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, urine albumin.
Discussed whether living alone is still safe; daughter is watching closely and has neurology again in August.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY
Date of service: 08/16/2023

Annual reassessment of Alzheimer disease, first evaluated here 08/2021. Her daughter attends.

Interval: attention has slipped further; bills are beyond her and she asks the same things over and over. Several times this spring she left a burner on, and once she could not find her way back from a neighbor's house a few doors down. The family describes her as quieter and more withdrawn, at times short-tempered, and she loses the thread of group conversation. No seizures, no hallucinations, no sudden step-downs.

Meds per list: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81. NKDA.
Social: never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: disoriented to time and place. Recalls none of three words after a delay. Clock drawing disorganized. Strength, sensation and coordination intact.

Labs: B12 and thyroid function normal.

Assessment: Alzheimer disease, progressive, now with safety issues at home.
Plan: stove shut-off device and supervision recommended; family considering more help at home. Follow up as needed or in 1 year.

Neurology

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter after the August neurology visit (letter reviewed; note their list again carries HCTZ - not taken since 2020). Stove knob covers installed. Daughter now there morning and evening.

Pt quieter today, answers briefly, smiles. Denies sadness when asked directly.
Weight 64, down about 10 kg over three years.

Exam: vitals as charted. SEM unchanged. Lungs clear. Feet intact.

A/P:
1. Alzheimer disease - progression per neurology; supervision increasing.
2. Weight loss with dementia - small frequent meals, nutrition shakes between meals.
3. DM - A1c today. Metformin continued.
4. HTN - fine.
Vaccines next month. RTC 3 months.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP and daughter's consent: high-dose flu L deltoid, updated Moderna R deltoid, RSV (Arexvy) L deltoid lower. Watched 15 minutes. Daughter to watch for fever or sore arms.
